transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood Solutions Eng), Tom (SparrowBridge VP Eng), Priya (Cloud Architect), Liam (Security Lead), Grace (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (note: rough):
SparrowBridge is evaluating Redwood for private VPC deployment. Primary concerns: CIDR conflicts, multi-region requirements (EU + US), private endpoints vs VPC peering, egress/egress inspection, KMS integration, and SOC2/ISO compliance. They want a short pilot: Dedicated-reserved pool in us-east-2 with private endpoints in eu-west-1 later.

Topics:
- Network onboarding flow (peering vs PrivateLink)
- IP addressing and overlapping CIDR mitigation
- Cross-account peering and transit options (TGW)
- Private endpoints, split-horizon DNS, and firewall rules
- KMS/HSM and audit logging integration
- Pilot scope and next steps

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan: "All right hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Jordan on the account side, with Samir and Elena from the infra team. How are you folks today?"
00:06 Tom: "Doing good, thanks. We wanted to use this as a workshop to nail down networking requirements — we've scrolled the docs but want the nitty gritty."
00:12 Priya: "Yep, I will mainly talk about our VPC layout and CIDRs. We have multiple accounts across AWS and GCP and some on-prem stuff."
00:18 Samir: "Perfect. On our side we'll explain the private deployment options. There's three common patterns: cross-account VPC peering, Transit Gateway-based routing, or PrivateLink / Private Endpoint approach depending on NAT/egress needs."
00:31 Priya: "We prefer not to route traffic across the open internet, so Private endpoints or VPC peering is a must. Also need control over egress inspection — our DLP and proxy teams require outbound traffic to traverse their appliances."
00:42 Elena: "Understood. For Redwood Private we support PrivateLink-style endpoints (we sometimes call them 'Private Endpoints' in docs) that create an ENI in your VPC, plus cross-account TGW/peering patterns. There's tradeoffs: PrivateLink gives control and DNS split-horizon but adds per-ENI work. Peering / TGW can be simpler for high-throughput but requires aligned CIDRs or NAT translation."
01:00 Liam: "Quick question — we have overlapping 10.0.0.0/16 ranges between a couple of our accounts. How do customers typically deal with that?"
01:08 Samir: "Good one. Typical approaches: renumbering is ideal but often infeasible. Folks either use TGW with route table fine-grained controls + NAT to map ranges, or use PrivateLink so each endpoint is per-account and avoids direct routing. Another pattern is a dedicated network router appliance that does 1:1 NAT for CIDR translation."
01:25 Grace: "We have a hardware firewall in our colo with BGP; would Redwood support connectivity via VPN or direct connect?"
01:31 Elena: "Yes, for on-prem we recommend either a site-to-site VPN or Direct Connect/Partner Interconnect and then advertise routes into the cloud, and Redwood can run in a VPC behind that connectivity. Important: make sure the maintenance window for the appliance is non-overlapping with any planned model rollouts if performance tests are scheduled."
01:52 Tom: "Region question: we must keep EU data in eu-west-1 for GDPR reasons. Can we run a Private deployment in eu-west-1 but still failover to us-east for non-personal workloads?"
02:02 Jordan: "Yes — you can pin model serving to region. Redwood supports regional deployment with routing policies — you could have a primary in eu-west-1 for EU traffic and a secondary in us-east for other workloads. We also support automatic fallback to a hosted variant if dedicated capacity isn't available, subject to compliance constraints."
02:19 Priya: "How does service discovery work across accounts? Split-horizon DNS?"
02:25 Samir: "We typically recommend split-horizon/private hosted zones. With PrivateLink endpoints, your route is internal and you can use private hosted zones that resolve to endpoint ENIs. For peering/TGW it's more manual: route tables, security groups, and sometimes central DNS resolvers (Route53 Resolver endpoints) are used."
02:47 Liam: "Encryption and KMS — we use a customer-managed KMS key. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?"
02:54 Elena: "Yes, Redwood Private supports CMKs. For on-prem HSM we usually have to do a bit more architecture work but the control plane can be configured to use your KMS for model artifact encryption and audit logging. We'll need an architecture review and possibly an addendum for HSM-backed keys."
03:14 Tom: "Audit logs and retention — our compliance team wants 1 year of network-level audit logs and SAML SSO for user access."
03:21 Jordan: "We can provide audit logs from the control plane and the console access logs, and integrate with your SIEM via syslog/S3 ingestion. SSO via SAML is supported; we also have RBAC to separate AE/SE/ops roles."
03:36 Grace: "Operational question — how do maintenance windows work? If Redwood applies kernel-level updates to the serving runtime will that cause downtime?"
03:44 Samir: "We run rolling updates across dedicated pools. For Dedicated deployments we honor configured maintenance windows and can do automatic failovers to standby capacity or hosted fallback depending on your SLA. We'll capture your maintenance constraints in the onboarding doc."
04:05 Priya: "Networking detail: what ports need to be open? Egress to the control plane? Outbound TLS?"
04:11 Elena: "Minimal: outbound 443 to the Redwood control plane endpoints for management, and the serving endpoints are internal across the VPC. If you use metrics/logs shipping to external services, you'll need egress to those endpoints. We'll provide a checklist with exact IP ranges and FQDNs; note some of our control plane endpoints use region-specific hostnames."
04:32 Tom: "About PrivateLink pricing and scaling — we run high throughput inference. Are there limits per ENI?"
04:39 Samir: "PrivateLink is fine for moderate throughput; if you have sustained heavy traffic TGW or peering with a Dedicated fleet is often more cost-effective. We'll run a cost/latency model during the pilot so you can compare. Also quantization and batching controls reduce egress and per-token costs."
04:58 Priya: "We'd like to do a 2-week pilot: spin up a small Dedicated pool in us-east-2, run a 48-hour throughput test, then evaluate adding an EU region. Is that feasible?"
05:06 Jordan: "Yes totally. Typical pilot: 2-4 GPU servers reserved for a short commit. We'll need a test token, sample prompts, and preferred time windows. Samir will coordinate the perf plan."
05:19 Samir: "I'll draft the perf test plan and include sequence lengths, concurrent connections, and token budgets. Also will include recommended quantization profiles so results are realistic."
05:28 Liam: "From a security posture: do you keep any PII in logs? What gets redacted?"
05:34 Elena: "By default, logs are result-level metadata, not full payloads. We can enable or disable transcript storage per tenant per the onboarding. For regulated customers we recommend disabling payload retention and using structured output or client-side redaction. We'll send the doc."
05:51 Tom: "One more — DNS and certificate management for private endpoints? We prefer our own certs."
05:57 Samir: "We can support your certificate authority for TLS termination at the edge when using a private endpoint. If you want mutual TLS for service-to-service within VPC, we can enable that as part of the Dedicated deployment."
06:10 Grace: "Any gotchas with GCP? We use Google Cloud in eu-west and their VPC peering has some limitations."
06:16 Elena: "GCP peering does not support transitive routing like AWS TGW. For GCP cross-project you may prefer Private Service Connect (PSC) endpoints. We have patterns for PSC and for cross-cloud architectures that use a central egress/VPN hub."
06:35 Priya: "Ok so next steps — can you send a diagram and checklist we can show the networking team?"
06:40 Jordan: "Yes. Action items we'll capture and send. Any blockers on your side for starting the pilot?"
06:45 Tom: "Internal sign-off from security but otherwise no exec blockers. Timeline: ideally start early April for the perf run."
06:52 Jordan: "Great. We'll target the perf cluster for week of April 6. Samir will reach out with the perf plan and provisioning checklist. Elena will send security docs and KMS notes. I'll send the peering/onboarding checklist and a sample CloudFormation/terraform snippet."
07:05 Priya: "One little callout: our compliance requires the control plane not to have PII, so need to confirm that hosted fallback wouldn't move EU personal data to US control plane."
07:14 Elena: "We'll flag that — hosted fallback can be disabled for accounts with data residency constraints. We'll note policy and doc an explicit 'no-hosted-fallback' option if needed."
07:26 Tom: "Perfect. Thanks, that's helpful."
07:30 Jordan: "Ok wrapping up — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the network deep dive if you want us to loop in your network folks. Anything else?"
07:36 Grace: "Nope that's it. Thanks everyone."
07:38 Jordan: "Thanks folks, meeting adjourned."

End transcript.
